articles.title: Alexander McQueen Minidress Set to be Auctioned by Christie's in December
articles.summary: The Alexander McQueen minidress from its 2010 "Plato's Atlantis" collection is one of the rarest and most technical masterpieces of high-end fashion, with an estimated price tag between $150,000 and $300,000.
articles.content: A highly prized Alexander McQueen minidress from its 2010 "Plato's Atlantis collection is set to be auctioned off by Christie's in December as part of its Luxury Week event. The multicolor silk garment is considered a rare and technical masterpiece, unlike the everyday clothing we see on runways. It will join other high-end fashion pieces at museums worldwide, but this time it will be up for grabs for a hefty price tag estimated to range between $150,000 and $300,000. According to Christie's head of handbags Max Brownawell, only a handful of these exact dresses were likely produced after the runway show, suggesting they are extremely rare. The Alexander McQueen collection Plato's Atlantis holds significant importance as it marked the final fully realized collection by the late designer himself. McQueen had previously stated that his previous collection was his last as a young man, but this collection took his vision to new heights with its bold and futuristic designs. The fourth look in the runway show, styled with iconic Armadillo boots, showcased the perfect blend of innovative style and craftsmanship. The dress's unique design features a sculpted drape covered in prints from the natural world, creating a stunning collage of abstracted imagery pulled from butterfly wings, snakeskin, and insects. This architectural approach to print placement is a testament to McQueen's exceptional skill as a designer. The piece still retains its original tag and has likely never been worn, making it an extremely rare find for fashion enthusiasts and collectors alike. The Alexander McQueen spring/summer 2010 show was groundbreaking in several ways, paving the way for future fashion events to push boundaries. This included being the first to be livestreamed in real time on the internet, allowing a wider audience to experience the spectacle remotely. It also marked a pioneering moment for music and fashion collaborations, with Lady Gaga's Bad Romance" premiering during the show's finale. The dress is now set to go under the hammer at Christie's inaugural fashion auction, which is expected to showcase significant designs. articles.title: Serie A: Inter Milan Struggle with Defensive Issues Under Coach Cristian Chivu
articles.summary: The 4-4 draw against Atalanta highlighted the defensive issues that have plagued Inter under coach Cristian Chivu.
articles.content: Serie A returned from its international break, and the first matchday of the new season brought a mix of excitement and concern for several teams. Atalanta's home game against Inter Milan ended in a stunning 4-4 draw, highlighting the defensive issues that have plagued the Nerazzurri under coach Cristian Chivu. The result was not surprising given Inter's struggles to shore up their defense, which has now conceded 17 goals in just 12 games. With such a porous backline, it's little wonder that Inter are struggling to assert themselves as title contenders. The team's inability to defend effectively is a major concern for the remainder of the season. Inter striker Francesco Pio Esposito had a memorable game, scoring a hat-trick against Atalanta, but even his impressive performance couldn't mask the team's defensive vulnerabilities. Despite having some of the league's top defenders on their roster, Inter have shown an alarming lack of cohesion and organization at the back. The 4-4 draw against Atalanta was a microcosm of Inter's season so far, full of moments of brilliance but also plagued by defensive lapses that ultimately cost them valuable points. With other teams like AS Roma, Napoli, Juventus, and AC Milan all posting convincing wins on the weekend, it's becoming increasingly clear that Inter will struggle to mount a serious challenge for the Serie A title. Inter's struggles are not just limited to their defense; they have also shown a lack of consistency in their performances throughout the season. With each passing game, it becomes more apparent that the team is in trouble and may be facing an uphill battle to salvage their season. articles.title: Oura Ring 5 Pricing and Alternatives
articles.summary: The Oura Ring 5 has been making waves in the health tracking market, but its hefty price tag and recurring fees have left some users looking for more affordable alternatives.
articles.content: The Oura Ring 5 has been making waves in the health tracking market, but its hefty price tag and recurring fees have left some users looking for more affordable alternatives. Oura's Ring 5 may start at $399, but that's just the beginning of the cost. To get the most out of this device, you'll need to shell out an additional $5.99 per month or $69.99 a year for a membership, which can add up quickly. The Oura Ring 5 has its advantages, including a sleek design and impressive week-long battery life, but some competitors offer similar features without the hefty price tag or monthly fees. One such competitor is Amazfit, whose Helio Ring offers a range of health tracking features at a significantly lower price point. Priced around $161, this ring monitors sleep, heart rate, and recovery via the Zepp app. The Helio Ring may have some compromises, however, including limited availability in sizes 8, 10, and 12, as well as battery life that tops out at just four days. Despite these limitations, the Amazfit Helio Ring is certainly an attractive option for those looking to ditch the Oura Ring's monthly fees and get a more affordable health tracking device. The LYNX smart ring from Renpho offers an alternative to the Oura Ring's hefty price tag, selling for $179.99 on sale from $199.99. This affordable option comes equipped with a portable charging case and supports both iOS and Android devices. It can track sleep, stress, and activity levels without requiring a subscription. However, initial testing has revealed some inconsistencies in the LYNX's performance. The heart-rate data during exercise was found to be unreliable, and the accuracy of sleep tracking was also questionable. Furthermore, the accompanying app provided limited analysis of the collected data, making it difficult to appreciate the value of the device despite its lower price. Another contender is the RingConn Gen 2 Air, priced at $199 with a claimed battery life of up to 10 days on a single charge. This smart ring offers heart rate, skin temperature, and sleep monitoring without any additional fees. However, it's worth noting that more advanced features like sleep apnea pattern monitoring are only available in pricier RingConn models. The Galaxy Ring from Samsung is an option for those with Android devices, although its price of $399.99 may be a deterrent for some. Currently listed on Amazon for $324.99, the savings are available but not immediate. The device comes with a charging case and doesn't require a subscription fee for health-tracking features. The Galaxy Ring's compatibility is limited to Samsung devices, and some AI features require a specific Samsung phone model. As such, iPhone users may find this option unsuitable due to its Android-only nature. The Circular Ring 2 offers a range of health monitoring features without requiring a subscription, including single-lead ECG readings and heart-rhythm monitoring. However, some advanced features do come with an additional fee, which may be off-putting for users who prefer not to incur extra costs. Despite its impressive hardware, the software has received criticism from reviewers, who have described the app as cluttered and slow to sync. Circular has since addressed these connectivity issues through updates, but potential buyers should be aware that the health measurements provided by the ring are not intended for medical diagnosis. This is a crucial distinction, especially for individuals with pre-existing conditions or those relying on accurate health data. In contrast, the Ultrahuman Ring Pro is priced at $479 and comes with a charging case and free core health tracking. However, some optional accessories known as PowerPlugs require an additional purchase. Reviewers have praised the ring's detailed app and battery life of around 10 days, but noted that automatic workout detection can sometimes fail to capture workouts. The Ring Pro has also been involved in a legal dispute with Oura, which sued Ultrahuman in October 2026 seeking to block US sales of the product. An earlier patent ruling had already prevented imports of the Ring Air, leaving some uncertainty around the future availability of this smart ring option. articles.title: Meat Temperature Before Cooking Not as Crucial as Thought
articles.summary: Experts are questioning the validity of letting meat sit out at room temperature before cooking, suggesting that this step may not be crucial for home cooks.
articles.content: A common cooking conundrum has many home cooks wondering: is it really necessary to let meat sit out at room temperature before cooking? The idea behind this step is that a warmer center will cook more evenly and prevent overcooking on the outside. However, food experts are now questioning its validity. According to Serge Krikorian, executive chef and co-owner of Vibrant Occasions Catering in Benton, Arkansas, "You don't need room-temperature meat to get a beautifully cooked dinner." He suggests that this step may not be as crucial as previously thought. Some recipes advise letting meat sit out for a short period before cooking, but experts warn that this can lead to food safety issues. A short counter rest may not significantly warm up thick cuts of meat, and waiting for large roasts to reach room temperature can create a problem. The notion that meat must be brought to room temperature before cooking has been a long-standing practice in culinary circles. However, experts suggest that this step may not be as crucial for home cooks as previously thought. According to Weidenaar, the benefits of tempering are relatively minor and may not be worth the extra time it takes. Restaurants often employ this technique out of necessity due to high volumes of orders and a need to manage cooking times efficiently. Grill cooks will typically remove steaks from storage and let them sit in a warm kitchen until they're ready to be grilled, allowing them to naturally warm up before being cooked. This approach is more about streamlining the cooking process than achieving optimal results. The idea behind tempering is that it gives the center of the meat an initial advantage, warming it up slightly before cooking begins. As Weidenaar explains, this can help prevent overcooking of the exterior during the cooking process. Cooking thick cuts of meat requires special attention to prevent overbrowning on the outside before the center is fully cooked. To achieve a good crust, it's crucial to pat dry excess moisture from the meat using paper towels, rather than relying solely on tempering it beforehand. This helps create an even cooking surface and prevents moisture from interfering with browning. Meat cooks unevenly when overcrowding the pan; experts recommend cooking in batches if necessary to ensure each piece has enough room to cook properly. When cooking any type of meat, food safety experts emphasize the importance of using a thermometer to ensure it reaches the recommended internal temperature for safe consumption. A short pause before cutting into the meat allows steam inside to condense back into liquid, preventing juices from escaping as you slice into it, according to Weidenaar. The resting period can also help retain moisture within the meat, although the optimal duration depends on the specific cut and its cooking method. articles.title: President Prabowo Subianto's Government Faces New Treason Allegations
articles.summary: Six current and former senior police officials have been named as suspects in the case.
articles.content: Indonesian authorities have taken a significant step in their ongoing investigation into an alleged treason plot against President Prabowo Subianto's government. Six current and former senior police officials have been named as suspects in the case. The move was announced by the National Police Criminal Investigation Agency, known as Bareskrim, during a news conference in Jakarta. The agency has been investigating allegations of illegal wiretapping targeting the president and other public figures since the beginning of this high-profile inquiry. At the center of the investigation is Gen. Listyo Sigit Prabowo, the former National Police chief who was allegedly trying to maintain his position for political purposes. He is accused of conspiring with five other senior officers to carry out acts of treason against the government. The suspects are alleged to have been motivated by a desire to weaken public trust in President Prabowo Subianto's administration. This, according to investigators, would have allowed them to exert greater influence over Indonesia's political landscape. The six suspects named in connection with the alleged treason plot include Gen. Listyo Sigit Prabowo and five other current and former senior officers: Slamet Uliandi , Eko Hadi Santoso , Ahrie Sonta Nasution, Iman Imanuddin and Tedjo Kusumo. The six suspects being investigated for alleged treason are facing multiple charges under Indonesia's Criminal Code, including conspiracy to overthrow the government. These serious offenses carry significant penalties, ranging from long prison terms to life imprisonment or even death. According to investigators, the suspects' alleged crimes involve ordering, participating in, or encouraging others to commit treasonous acts with a clear intention of undermining the president's authority and governance. This could potentially render the president unable to govern effectively. Investigations have also revealed connections between some of the suspects and recent large-scale anti-government demonstrations held across Indonesia. Authorities have seized various items during these protests, including 20 One Piece flags that have become a symbol of resistance among some Indonesian protesters. The flags are part of a Japanese anime and manga franchise that has gained popularity in Indonesia, where it is seen as a representation of defiance against the government. Investigators are looking into whether the suspects were involved in organizing or supporting these activities, which are now under scrutiny. Safrudin stated that investigators are tracing the activities supported by the suspects to determine if they had any influence on other political movements aimed at weakening the government. articles.title: Moss Ant Colonies Defy Traditional Expectations with Winged and Wingless Queens
articles.summary: A new study has found that queen ants can be either winged or wingless, challenging the idea of strict caste roles in a species typically characterized by physical characteristics.
articles.content: A groundbreaking study has shed light on the surprising diversity of moss ant colonies, where queen ants can be either winged or wingless, defying traditional expectations about their physical characteristics. The researchers, based at Harvard University and the University of Georgia, set out to understand what drives this variation in a species that typically follows strict caste roles. By examining 173 colonies from across Canada and the United States, they aimed to uncover the underlying factors influencing queen ant morphology. A significant aspect of this study was the collection and examination of over a thousand individual ants, including workers, winged queens, and wingless queens. The researchers meticulously measured various features such as body size, head size, and eye size to identify any patterns or correlations between these characteristics and queen type. The data revealed that wingless queens exhibited a unique blend of worker-like and queen-like traits. Specifically, their mid-body sections were more similar in height to those of workers, while their relative eye length was comparable to that of winged queens. This finding provided valuable insight into the physical differences between winged and wingless queens. To further investigate this phenomenon, the scientists analyzed the DNA of 25 winged queens and 28 wingless queens. Their analysis uncovered a striking pattern: 80 genetic variations were consistently present in all wingless queens but absent from their winged counterparts. The discovery of a supergene responsible for determining whether a moss ant queen is winged or wingless has led researchers to uncover more about its role in caste development. This supergene, named ergatoid after the scientific term for wingless queens, contains around 6.5 million DNA building blocks and is located on chromosome 1. The team's analysis confirmed that it was a dominant variant, meaning just one copy was enough for a queen to develop without wings. Further testing of additional ant queens revealed that this supergene is consistently present in all wingless queens but absent from their winged counterparts. The researchers' findings have shed new light on the developmental process of queens. Instead of turning ordinary worker larvae into queens, the supergene alters the development of those already destined to become queens. Changes in gene activity suggest that hormones involved in regulating development and growth may play a role in how the supergene affects queen development. However, the exact mechanisms behind this process remain unclear for now. The discovery of a single supergene that determines whether a moss ant queen is winged or wingless has left scientists intrigued about the underlying mechanisms. This supergene, which was identified in research published in Science Advances, appears to have a profound impact on the development of queen-destined larvae. According to the findings, the presence of this supergene can lead to the formation of a novel caste in ants, one that is distinct from both winged and wingless queens. The implications of this discovery are far-reaching, but for now, the exact mechanisms behind this process remain unclear for now, leaving scientists with more questions than answers. articles.title: Wasps Recognize Faces of Nestmates through Neural Correlates
articles.summary: A new study published in the journal Cell has found that wasps use a distinct group of brain cells to recognize individual faces.
articles.content: Research from Wake Forest University has shed light on how wasps recognize the faces of their nestmates, a skill shared by humans in distinguishing friends from foes and loved ones. The study, led by Christopher Jernigan, assistant professor of biology, offers new insights into how animals process social visual information to distinguish one face from another. This research is part of a broader effort to understand the neural mechanisms behind facial recognition across species. The findings have implications for understanding human behavior as well. Jernigan's team collaborated with researchers at Cornell University to investigate the neural correlates of facial recognition in wasps. Their work appears in the journal Cell, where they present their study titled "Neural correlates of facial recognition in a social wasp." The study's findings reveal that a distinct group of brain cells responds to images of other wasps, enabling them to recognize individual faces. Researchers have been studying Polistes fuscatus, also known as the northern paper wasp, which is found in colonies across eastern and central North America, from southern Canada through Florida and Texas. These small animals build complex nests under building eaves and on porch ceilings. Their papery, umbrella-shaped structures are made up of hexagonal cells. Facial recognition plays a crucial role in maintaining social order within the wasp colony, particularly among females who establish a hierarchy. By recognizing individual faces, they can avoid constant conflicts for dominance and maintain day-to-day social harmony without needing to constantly battle each other. The use of facial recognition by these wasps raises interesting questions about the evolution of this ability across different species, including humans. The ability of paper wasps to distinguish between different faces is a remarkable feat considering their tiny brain size, equivalent to that of a grain of rice. This complex task of recognizing and remembering individual faces requires significant cognitive processing power, yet these wasps are capable of achieving it with ease. Their social behavior also reveals another fascinating aspect of their ability to recognize each other. When two unknown wasps engage in combat, a third wasp can observe the outcome and adjust its behavior accordingly upon meeting one of them. This is known as social eavesdropping, where the observer wasp learns from the conflict between others to inform its own interactions. The researchers involved in this study have provided valuable insights into the social lives of paper wasps. Despite their relatively simple vision system, these wasps exhibit complex social dynamics that are centered around their ability to recognize one another. This specialized capacity allows them to establish dominance hierarchies within their nests through a series of conflicts and interactions. The next stage in this research will be to explore the nuances of facial recognition in paper wasps, including whether they can distinguish between different facial expressions. This will provide further understanding into the evolution of this ability across various species, including humans. The study of wasp facial recognition has revealed a surprising similarity to human-like abilities. This ability is remarkable in its own right, and the fact that it involves neural computations similar to those used by humans is almost unbelievable. The sheer number of neural connections required to achieve this task is a testament to the complexity of insect cognition. The discovery highlights the intricate social structures found within wasp colonies, where individual recognition plays a crucial role in maintaining order and cooperation. articles.title: Low-Cost Cancer Screening Test Developer Dies at 95
articles.summary: Renowned biochemist Bruce Ames left an indelible mark on the scientific community before his passing at 95.
articles.content: Renowned biochemist Bruce Ames left an indelible mark on the scientific community before his passing at 95. His most notable contribution was developing a low-cost screening test for cancer-causing substances, which earned him widespread recognition in his field. However, Ames devoted the latter part of his career to exploring a lesser-known area: the role of nutrients in promoting healthy ageing. The idea that there may be a class of unrecognised longevity vitamins and proteins is not new; Ames had been researching it for years before his 2022 paper on the subject. In fact, he wrote in one of his last papers that "many as-yet-unknown longevity vitamins and proteins likely remain to be discovered". This assertion has sparked interest among researchers who are now investigating several promising candidates, including those found in mushrooms and seaweed. These substances have long been associated with health benefits, but the question remains whether they can actually promote healthy ageing. Proving the long-term effects of dietary factors is a notoriously difficult task, and the field of anti-ageing supplements has a history of failed promises. Yet, if Ames's hypothesis holds true, we may be on the cusp of discovering new ways to support our bodies' natural processes. A healthy diet requires essential micronutrients for basic metabolic reactions, around 30 vitamins and minerals in total. These include vitamins from A to K and minerals like calcium and iron, which are crucial for immediate survival. Without them, we risk developing conditions such as scurvy, rickets, and beriberi. But Ames's work suggests that even with adequate intake of these essential micronutrients, our bodies may still suffer long-term damage due to inadequate allocation. He proposed in 2006 that when vitamins and minerals are scarce, our bodies operate a triage system, prioritising immediate survival functions over others like DNA repair and mitochondria maintenance. When vitamins and minerals are scarce, our bodies may not just prioritize immediate survival functions but also allocate limited resources to less urgent tasks like DNA repair and mitochondria maintenance. The scarcity of certain nutrients can have far-reaching consequences, including an increased risk of cancer and cardiovascular disease. Moderate deficiencies in vitamin D, for instance, have been linked to these conditions. Bruce Ames' subsequent research with Joyce McCann at the Children's Hospital Oakland Research Institute in California revealed that selenium and vitamin K are indeed preferentially allocated when they are scarce, focusing on biological systems crucial for short-term survival. The renowned biochemist continued working into his 90s, driven by a desire to uncover dietary substances that promote healthy ageing. This inquiry led him to propose the existence of an entire class of unrecognised nutrients with protective pathways in our bodies. These compounds, Ames suggested, could fine-tune metabolism and shield us from insidious long-term damage if consumed in sufficient quantities. His 2022 paper listed around 40 key ingredients for thousands of chemical reactions that he believed were critical for preventing chronic conditions and promoting longevity. Ames proposed a dual function for many known vitamins and minerals: besides supporting immediate survival functions, they could also delay the ageing process. He also suggested that other dietary biochemicals, not officially recognised as vitamins or with age-delaying properties, may have a positive impact on lifespan. The sheer number of biochemicals in our food is staggering, but we know surprisingly little about their potential impacts on our bodies. This "nutritional dark matter" includes over 250 chemicals listed in various databases as potentially being able to alter the ageing process, according to an academic book on Supplements and Drugs for Healthy Longevity. Studies on longevity nutrients often rely on experiments using organisms such as yeasts and worms to test their effects. However, according to Suresh Rattan, a biogerontologist at Aarhus University in Denmark, strong evidence of these nutrients' impact on humans is still lacking. Rattan co-edited an academic book that notes this gap in knowledge. The book highlights the need for more human studies to confirm the potential benefits of longevity nutrients. But new research and clinical trials are underway to identify nutrients that may slow down ageing, providing hope for a deeper understanding of their effects on humans. One such trial is the DO-HEALTH study, which began in 2025. This randomised controlled trial involved 777 healthy individuals aged over 70 who received either vitamin D, omega-3 fatty acids, or a home exercise programme to assess their impact on disease prevention and longevity. The results showed that participants who took omega-3 supplements experienced moderate slowing of biological ageing, while those who combined it with vitamin D or exercise saw additional benefits. Although the study did not measure healthspan directly, the number of years we live in good health, its authors pointed out that even small changes in biological ageing could have significant effects on population health. Researchers are now focusing on several overlooked nutrients that may play a significant role in promoting longevity. These candidates include carotenoids and certain antioxidants produced by bacteria and fungi, which have been proposed as potential keys to extending healthspan. In Singapore, where a third of the population is expected to be over 65 by 2050, initiatives are underway to investigate these nutrients further. The country's demographic shift has led to a surge in healthcare costs due to rising rates of conditions such as cancer and dementia. To combat this trend, large-scale investment is being poured into clinical trials exploring new ways to elongate healthspan. Among the nutrients under scrutiny is ergothioneine, an antioxidant highlighted by biochemist Bruce Ames three decades ago. Ergothioneine is produced mainly by fungi and bacteria, with mushrooms being the richest dietary source of this nutrient. Research has shown that eating a diet rich in mushrooms can lead to a longer life expectancy, possibly due to their high antioxidant content. This evidence has led scientists like Halliwell to believe that maintaining even small levels of ergothioneine in the bloodstream is crucial for brain health. Halliwell's hypothesis is that ergothioneine should be considered a vital nutrient, just like vitamins C and D. He suggests that not having enough ergothioneine could lead to noticeable symptoms, unlike other nutrients where deficiencies are often gradual. A pilot study by Halliwell and his colleagues aimed to test this theory, enrolling people over 60 with mild cognitive impairment in a year-long trial of ergothioneine supplements. Although the study was cut short due to the COVID-19 pandemic, it still showed promising results, including improved memory and learning abilities, as well as slowed neuron damage. Halliwell has secured funding to restart the full-scale trial, which will provide more conclusive evidence for his hypothesis. In the UK, another trial is underway, focusing on ergothioneine's potential to boost the immune system in midlife by reducing senescent white blood cells and chronic inflammation. Scientists are exploring the potential of fucoidan, a compound found in brown seaweed, to activate genes that promote DNA repair and slow down ageing. A clinical trial involving 60 Singaporeans aged 50-80 with signs of pre-frailty is underway to investigate whether daily doses of four grams of fucoidan can have a positive impact on their health. The researchers will monitor the participants' inflammatory and immune signals, as well as their DNA, to assess whether fucoidan can slow down ageing. In addition to these tests, they will also examine the participants' body composition, muscle quality, sleep patterns, cognition, and skin health. Researchers are optimistic that the trial will provide valuable insights into the potential benefits of fucoidan, with one expert suggesting that eating more brown seaweed could be beneficial for overall health. Other researchers are working to identify overlooked compounds in food that might have a significant impact on our well-being. In Japan, scientists have identified a cholesterol-lowering chemical called meglutol found in fermented soya beans, which could potentially rival the effects of statins. The discovery of meglutol highlights the importance of further research into unrecognised nutrients in our food and their potential benefits for human health. This study demonstrates that even seemingly ordinary foods can hold secrets to improving our quality of life. Research into these compounds holds promise for the development of new treatments or supplements, but much more work is needed to fully understand their effects on human health. The findings from these studies could have a significant impact on public health, potentially leading to new dietary recommendations and improved treatment options for various age-related diseases. articles.title: Sanae Takaichi Snubbed by China at APEC Summit
articles.summary: Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi faced an unexpected obstacle upon arrival at the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) summit in Shenzhen, China.
articles.content: Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi recently found herself snubbed by China at the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) summit in Shenzhen, signaling a possible deterioration in bilateral ties. Upon arrival on November 18, Takaichi faced an unexpected obstacle when the mobile stairs leading to her aircraft were not long enough, forcing her to hold onto the door frame for support as she stepped down from the plane. The modest reception awaiting Takaichi upon reaching the airport tarmac stood out in contrast to the more elaborate welcomes extended to other APEC leaders. Unlike many of their counterparts, Japan's delegation did not receive any musical performances or traditional dances. Japan's Yomiuri newspaper reported that during a dinner meeting with Chinese leader Xi Jinping on November 20, "his reaction was cold." This lack of enthusiasm from Xi towards Takaichi marked an unusually frosty encounter between the two leaders. William Yang, a Taiwan-based analyst for the International Crisis Group, observed that China's chilly demeanor towards Japan was evident as soon as Takaichi's plane touched down. Takaichi's arrival in Beijing was met with an awkward silence, according to observers. The contrast between her reception and that of other world leaders was stark. The tensions on display were a reflection of the complex history between China and Japan. This legacy of conflict is deeply ingrained, with Chinese schoolchildren learning about the atrocities committed by Japanese forces during their occupation of key cities in the 1930s. Japanese officials argue that their country's post-war efforts to make amends have been consistently overlooked. These include repeated apologies and significant economic aid that helped China become a major economic power today. Japan's relationship with China has been strained for several years due to various issues, including China's growing military spending and assertive stance over disputed territories. The breakdown of talks over the East China Sea in 2006 marked a significant turning point, as did the resurgence of nationalism following the Beijing Olympics in 2008. Chinese submarine activity near Japanese waters has also raised concerns among defence analysts. This heightened tension was further exacerbated by China's claims to the Senkaku Islands. Japan's leaders have been cautious in their dealings with China, but the situation took a dramatic turn in November 2025 when the Japanese leader made a statement that sparked Beijing's ire. The statement implied that any conflict involving Taiwan would inevitably compromise Japan's national security. Beijing responded swiftly and severely to this perceived provocation, demanding that the Japanese leader retract his words. In addition to diplomatic pressure, China imposed economic sanctions on Japan by restricting exports of rare earth minerals critical to its industry. China's stance is seen as a significant departure from previous episodes where ruffled national feelings were smoothed over with reciprocal goodwill gestures. Beijing appears to believe it has more leverage in the current situation, according to observers. Beijing's leverage in the current situation has grown significantly due to its control over vital resources. Japan relies heavily on China for rare earths, a crucial component in many high-tech products. This dependence gives Beijing considerable influence over Tokyo's actions. A visible military presence around Japan, sometimes in cooperation with Russia, adds to China's bargaining power. The US administration's urging of Tokyo to de-escalate tensions has also contributed to the current dynamics. Washington's approach suggests that it is not willing to firmly back its ally at this time. This may embolden Beijing to maintain a hardline stance. The consequences for Japan could be severe, with potential repercussions on its economy and security. Takaichi's position is precarious due to her own commitments as a conservative leader. She has spoken out against China's military expansion in the South China Sea and its pressure on Taiwan. Giving in to Beijing's demands would risk alienating her hardline supporters. This dilemma makes it difficult for her to find a middle ground that satisfies both her domestic base and the international community. The analyst Yang notes that Takaichi is walking a tightrope between reducing tensions with China and preparing Japan for potential contingencies over Taiwan. Her ability to navigate this complex situation will be put to the test in the coming days. The stakes are high, with significant implications for both Japan's domestic politics and its international relationships. Beijing's approach is likely to continue unchanged, with targeted exports and diplomatic pressure being used to assert its influence. This could include further cooperation with Russia and North Korea on issues related to Japan's security. The situation remains fluid, with many variables at play. The decision by Japan to snub China at the APEC summit has left many wondering what's next for their strained relations. Analysts believe that Japan will likely seek opportunities to improve ties in exchange for small concessions from China. However, a reset in the dynamics between the two countries depends on how the Trump administration shapes its foreign policy in the remaining time of his presidency. The situation remains fluid, with many variables at play. The complex interdependence between China and Japan makes full decoupling unlikely, according to some experts. Trade, technology, and critical minerals are now seen as security issues that will prevent a return to isolating politics from economics. A new power bloc is emerging, but the West should not be overly concerned about this development. articles.content: Apple has released an update for its HomePod speakers that adds a new feature called Sound Glow to its lineup of smart speakers. The top of the speaker now comes alive with a colorful light show synchronized to the music playing on it, creating a visually engaging experience for users. This feature was introduced alongside the launch of the HomePod mini 2 and is available on all current models, including the original HomePod mini and the larger HomePod 2. The update makes better use of the existing lights on top of the speaker, which were previously only used to indicate when Siri was listening or a song was playing. HomePods have a basic set of lights that don't offer much beyond indicating activity, but with Sound Glow, users can enjoy a more immersive experience while listening to music. The new feature uses an array of LEDs on top of the speaker to create a colorful display that mirrors the rhythm and beat of the music. Users who want to try out Sound Glow will need to check their HomePod settings to see if it's available for their device. The latest software update for HomePods has brought a new feature called Sound Glow, which utilizes the speaker's LEDs to create a more engaging listening experience. When playing music, HomePods now incorporate colors from album art into a pulsing light display that synchronizes with the song's beat, making each track visually distinct. For example, Taylor Swift's The Life of a Showgirl will be accompanied by predominantly green and orange lights, while Miley Cyrus's Endless Summer Vacation will result in blue hues on your HomePod. This dynamic light animation is said to react in real time to the bass and treble levels of each song, ensuring that even two tracks from the same album will have unique visual effects. To activate Sound Glow on your HomePods, ensure that all devices connected to it are running the latest software. This includes not just the HomePods themselves but also any Apple device paired with them. Users can verify this by checking for updates in the Home app from another compatible device. A HomePod running the latest software will automatically update after a period of time, but users can speed up the process by manually confirming an update is available. This involves tapping on the three-dot button within the Home app and selecting Home Settings. To use Sound Glow with your HomePods, you'll need an Apple Intelligence-enabled device paired with them. This includes iPhones from the 15 Pro model onwards, iPads running the latest operating system, or Mac devices equipped with the M1 chip or newer. For those who prefer to watch their music, an Apple TV running tvOS 27 can also enable Sound Glow on HomePods. To activate Sound Glow on your HomePod, ensure that your device is updated to its latest version. This will allow you to access the feature and enjoy a synchronized light display with music. Go back to the Home app's main screen and tap on your HomePod icon, then navigate to Settings by scrolling down and locating the Sound Glow toggle. Simply flip it on, repeating this process for each individual HomePod if necessary. If you decide that Sound Glow isn't to your liking, turning it off requires a similar sequence of actions, but with the toggle flipped in the opposite direction. articles.title: Nepal's Prime Minister Balendra Shah Embarks on First Official Visit to India
articles.summary: Nepal's new Prime Minister Balendra Shah has begun his first official visit to India, marking a shift in Nepal's diplomatic landscape. His background as a rapper-turned-politician makes him an unusual figure in Kathmandu's politics.
articles.content: Nepal's new Prime Minister Balendra Shah has embarked on his first official visit to India, marking a significant shift in the country's diplomatic landscape. This week's trip is a departure from the norm, as Nepal's leaders have traditionally been seasoned politicians rather than fresh faces. Shah's background as a young rapper-turned-politician makes him an unusual figure in Kathmandu's politics. His strong electoral mandate has given him a unique position to shape Nepal's relationship with its southern neighbor and largest trading partner, India. Shah's visit is expected to focus on the pressing issues facing his country. Nepal's economic strain and recent devastating flash floods have created an urgent need for investment and support from India. The Nepalese public is eagerly awaiting tangible results from Shah's diplomatic efforts, particularly in terms of job creation, infrastructure development, and improved governance at home. To achieve this, Shah must establish a strong rapport with Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi. Despite the two countries' shared border, cultural heritage, and historical ties, their relationship has been complicated by territorial disputes and Nepal's desire to be recognized as an equal partner. Constantino Xavier, a senior fellow at the Center for Social and Economic Progress in New Delhi, cautions against expecting too much from this visit alone. Shah's meeting with Modi is seen as a crucial step towards safeguarding Nepal's flood recovery efforts and fostering development. The success of his trip will depend on his ability to navigate the complexities of Nepal-India relations and strike a balance between addressing pressing issues and managing expectations. Nepal's new prime minister has emphasized the need for sustained economic cooperation in his country's relations with India. He believes that such cooperation should be at the forefront of bilateral ties because it directly contributes to the socioeconomic development of both nations. This approach is expected to yield tangible benefits, including addressing pressing issues and meeting local expectations. The young leader faces a significant challenge in converting his domestic electoral mandate and goodwill towards New Delhi into concrete economic gains. He must also tackle longstanding border disputes and rectify a massive trade imbalance between the two countries. The prime minister's administration has identified diplomacy as a key strategy for advancing Nepal's development aspirations, which was reflected in recent bilateral talks with Indian Prime Minister Modi. During these talks, both sides focused on promoting economic cooperation through various channels. These include engaging in trade, investment, connectivity, and infrastructure development initiatives. Kathmandu sought financial support from New Delhi to aid in the reconstruction efforts following the devastating floods that ravaged Nepal last August. The disaster claimed over 1,450 lives and left thousands missing or unaccounted for. The scale of destruction was staggering, with roads, bridges, hydropower projects, and settlements being swept away by the floods. The estimated cost of reconstruction is around $4.8 billion, which prompted Kathmandu to prioritize securing Indian financial assistance. In response, Modi announced a package of $1.63 billion to help rebuild flood-hit areas and upgrade other infrastructure projects. This aid includes around $380 million as a grant and the rest as a concessional loan. The agreement reached between Nepal and India during Prime Minister Shah's visit has far-reaching implications for their economic relationship. Deepening cooperation in various sectors, including trade and investment, is expected to boost bilateral ties. A new long-term vision aims to strengthen economic integration and development between the two nations. Key areas of focus include broadening educational and innovation partnerships, as well as enhancing energy and infrastructure cooperation. Improved market access and trade links will also be crucial for Nepal's economic growth. Furthermore, India has committed to providing additional air and port access to landlocked Nepal, increasing its connectivity with the rest of the world. The visit marked a significant shift in the high-level exchange between the two countries, which had been periodically strained by political mistrust and territorial disputes. The strategic Himalayan territory of Kalapani, Lipulekh, and Limpiyadhura remains a contentious issue, with both nations holding competing claims. Nepal's Prime Minister Shah has taken a pragmatic approach to his India visit, steering clear of sensitive issues like border disputes. As mayor of Kathmandu, he had previously raised these concerns, which contributed significantly to his nationalist image and broader political agenda. Former Foreign Minister Bimala Rai Paudyal believes that the new government's focus on economic issues may be a strategic move to address long-standing bilateral problems. However, she also expressed concern that the border disputes remain unresolved, posing a significant strain on their relations. The success of Nepal's new Prime Minister's visit to India will be measured by the establishment of a stable and mutually beneficial relationship between the two countries. This would involve addressing long-standing territorial disputes, concerns over the 1950 Treaty of Peace and Friendship, and Nepal's economic dependence on its southern neighbor. To fully capitalize on its geographical location, Nepal should not feel pressured to choose between India and China, but rather leverage its position to secure economic and diplomatic benefits from both. The Prime Minister has a unique opportunity to transform Nepal's strategic vulnerability into an asset that brings prosperity and influence. The implementation of agreements announced during the visit will be crucial in determining whether a tangible reset on the economic front is achieved. Ultimately, it will require a willingness from both governments to address disputes that have strained ties for years, paving the way for more predictable and beneficial cooperation.
